mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened financing conditions for corporations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS increase is not confirmed by at least two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 1,000 over three consecutive months coincides with a negative S&P 500 forward 60-day return as investor sentiment deteriorates on labor market weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >1,000 over three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period, the 60-day forward returns remain positive whenever the three-month PAYEMS increase threshold is met, or unemployment falls sharply after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the following month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive as the Fed is likely to pause or reverse rate hikes, boosting equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL surprises above +3% in the next month
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive inflation surprise months above +3%, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05), or the Fed raises rates regardless.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 5% followed by a decline of 2% in the next month signals a supply-side shock, predicting a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥5% then falls by ≥2% in consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such cycles, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the pattern is not confirmed by at least two independent economic shocks (e.g., oil price spike).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates rate cuts and easier financing.
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the 20-day forward returns do not outperform the prior 20-day average during the FEDFUNDS below 4% regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in job openings (RSAFS) by more than 20% coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market tightness softens and equity risk appetite improves.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >20% in a single month
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to baseline (Rank IC < 0.1), or job openings do not revert upward after the drop.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% each month suggest dual demand and supply pressures, predicting a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
error_note: Demand interaction scenario constructed using proxy proxies for demand and labor.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by ≥2% AND INDPRO falls by ≥2% in the same month, repeated for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 8 such contraction cycles, the 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of declining unemployment (UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates a robust labor market and policy easing.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE < 4% for ≥6 months, the 20-day forward returns are not consistently positive (t-test p > 0.05 across all such regimes).
